stem: A cricket academy in Karachi has 40 players, and all of them took part in a study. The coach randomly assigned 20 of the players to practice a new batting drill and the other 20 to practice the usual drill. After two months, the players who practiced the new drill had a greater average increase in batting average. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?

choices.A: The new drill likely causes a greater increase in batting average for all cricket players in Pakistan.
choices.B: No cause-and-effect conclusion can be drawn, because the players were not selected at random from all players in Pakistan.
choices.C: The new drill likely caused a greater increase in batting average for the players at this academy.
choices.D: The study shows only an association, because the coach decided which players were in the study.

solution: The players were randomly assigned to the two drills, so a cause-and-effect conclusion is supported.
Every player at the academy took part, so the conclusion applies to the academy's players, but not to players elsewhere.

explanation.A: Incorrect. The players all came from one academy, so the result cannot be generalized to all players in Pakistan.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Random selection is needed to generalize, not to conclude cause and effect; random assignment supports cause and effect here.
explanation.C: Correct. Random assignment supports cause and effect for the academy's players, who were all in the study.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The coach decided who was in the study, but the drills were assigned at random, which supports cause and effect.
